lede: Detroit had last change, so Todd McLellan picked most of these matchups. Detroit played without William Wallinder. Boston played without Frédéric Brunet and Michael Eyssimont.

notes.head: The fourth line drew Kastelic’s line
notes.text: Todd McLellan sent Rasmussen, Dries and Kolesar out for 6:14 of their 8:37 at 5-on-5 against Jeannot, Kastelic and Kuraly (72%, about 21% with no line matching).

notes.head: Raymond’s line drew Pastrňák’s line
notes.text: Brandsegg-Nygård, Copp and Raymond spent 10:01 of their 15:44 at 5-on-5 against Pastrňák, E. Lindholm and Geekie (64%, about 28% with no line matching), and they had the better of the chances, 0.33 to 0.19 expected goals. The only Detroit goal came then.

notes.head: DeBrincat’s line drew Zacha’s line
notes.text: DeBrincat, Finnie and Kasper spent 8:17 of their 16:15 at 5-on-5 against Peterka, Zacha and Mittelstadt (51%, about 27% with no line matching), and they had the better of the chances, 0.27 to 0.11 expected goals.

notes.head: One matchup went wrong
notes.text: Mazur, Compher and Arvidsson kept drawing Boston’s third line, Poitras, Minten and Khusnutdinov. In those 5:32 Boston had 0.50 expected goals to Detroit’s 0.02.

foot: Todd McLellan matched about as hard as in his other home games: each line spent 56% of its time against one opposing line, against 33% to 54% in his last ten.
